correctness.rationale: Under strictly positive incident-edge additive valuations, an orientation violates zero-inclusive EFX exactly when an oriented edge u->v has at least two incoming edges at v and utility at u smaller than its edge weight. The all-unit case forbids isolated alternating triples (+-+) and (-+-), and a 4-state transfer matrix with characteristic polynomial (x²-x-1)(x²-x+1) gives L_n+2cos(n pi/3). The heavy exceptional edge removes a specified first/last-run position; the light case removes next-to-last/second run positions, and cyclic shifts biject the exclusions. The remaining trace 2(T^n)_{++,++}=F_{n+1}+delta_n follows from Cayley-Hamilton and initial values. Binet yields the positive discontinuous limiting loss. Independently enumerated every orientation for n=4..10 at weights 1/2,1,3/2, using direct every-agent/every-removal EFX inequalities, agreeing with the formulas. Finite enumeration does not prove all n.
residual_risks: Strict positivity tau>0 and zero-inclusive rather than positive-only EFX is essential.
No result for two or more perturbed edges, nonincident valuations, or arbitrary graphs.

originality.rationale: The primary 2025 Zeng–Mehta EFX paper proves strong orientability and complexity, including bipartite existence, but not a weighted single-edge exact orientation census. Earlier published path and multicycle enumerators involve different host graphs or parallel-edge goods, and the classical binary-run count by itself is not a new claim. The proved finite and asymptotic fairness-sensitivity transfer is a natural additional statement. Historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Equivalent fair-orientation counts could exist under a different graph-allocation convention; exact zero-inclusive definition must match.
Some elementary binary-run enumerations are classical; no novelty is claimed for those alone.

value.rationale: The number and prevalence of EFX outcomes are natural questions distinct from existence. A single arbitrarily weak positive edge-weight perturbation removes asymptotically 27.64 percent of fair orientations on the canonical sparse cycle family, an exact nonperturbative structural sensitivity. The conclusion is motivated by robustness of fair allocations and is not merely a raw Fibonacci identity.
residual_risks: Only labeled full simple-cycle orientations with common positive endpoint valuations are treated.

limitations: n>=4, exactly one edge has weight tau>0 different from the unit edge weights.
